approach.1.body: Identify the advance, remittance basis, payment schedule and repayment target. A cap factor describes a target—not an annual interest rate.
approach.1.title: Start with the contract.
approach.2.body: Inspect stable trading, declining sales and closure scenarios. Observe how the specified payment rules respond under the model’s assumptions.
approach.2.title: Change the revenue path.
approach.3.body: Consider seller payment burden alongside provider recovery. Payment as a share of revenue does not establish affordability; incomplete target recovery is not a default prediction.
approach.3.title: Read both sides.
approach.lead: A financing contract connects payments to a business that changes over time. RBF examines that connection without treating a model as evidence of what real merchants will do.

demo.arg.1.body: Where a seller's bureau history is thin, order data, customer ratings and delivery performance still accumulate continuously. Whether those predict repayment is not a claim this project tests — it has no seller outcomes to test against, and no comparison against bureau data was performed.

demo.arg.2.body: The shipped prototype takes merchant-submitted figures and does not connect to any platform API. Reading revenue directly from platforms is the design intent, not the current behaviour — so today these values are self-reported, which is exactly what the integrity screen exists to test.

demo.arg.3.body: Repayment is a percentage of revenue, not a fixed installment — a slow month lengthens the term rather than raising the payment. It does not remove the risk: permanent revenue cessation before completion, while a balance is still outstanding, can prevent the cap from ever being reached.

demo.how.2.body: The active scorer produces an unvalidated demo risk score and per-signal flags. When the model artifact loads, that is a Random Forest and Logistic Regression ensemble, trained on synthetic data whose label is a formula over the same features; when it does not, a deterministic heuristic runs instead. Neither path has measured predictive validity, and the score carries no predictive claim. The score sets the risk tier, and the tier sets the advance, remittance rate, cap factor and eligibility — so the active scorer can change the terms shown.

figure.shape.interruption.desc: With eligible revenue at zero, the revenue-share payment is zero. Restarting revenue can restart payments; reaching the repayment target is not assured.
figure.shape.steady.desc: With revenue unchanged, both indexed payments stay level. This diagram does not compare their monetary amounts.

lab.hero.question: Research question. When a seller's revenue falls, how does the burden of a fixed instalment differ from a revenue share — and what does that flexibility cost the financier in recovery speed?
